title: Metric-driven degradation policy for hosted endpoints — PRD + launch checklist
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define an operational policy and acceptance criteria for automatically and manually degrading hosted inference endpoints under sustained platform stress (latency, GPU pressure, regional outage) while preserving correctness, visibility, and safe rollback. This PRD covers telemetry thresholds, automated routing fallback, graceful quality degradation profiles (e.g., token cap, truncation, cheaper model substitution), customer-visible signals, and the launch checklist for the hosted API surface.
goals: Provide a standardized, metric-driven degradation policy for hosted endpoints that prevents total outages while limiting customer impact.
Ship guardrails that tie directly to observability: specific metric thresholds, automated mitigations, and post-degrade analysis.
Ensure launch readiness with tests, runbooks, and canary validation against production-like workloads.
non_goals: Automated model-level hallucination mitigation (out of scope for initial rollout).
Replacing customer-configured rollout policies for Dedicated/Private customers. Those will be integrated in later phases.
On-prem air-gapped deployment support — follow-up project.
acceptance_criteria: Policy implemented in routing layer and console toggle exists to enable/disable auto-degrade per-customer.
Telemetry: latency_p95 > 2x baseline OR queue_depth > 1500 triggers degradation path within configured 60s window.

Degradation actions validated: (a) fall back to smaller model variant, (b) enforce per-request token limit, (c) enable fast-path truncation — each action must be reversible automatically when metrics return to normal.
SLOs preserved: during graceful degradation event, error_rate must remain < 1% and tail latency p99 must be bounded (documented in runbook).
Customer notifications emitted via status page and in-console banner with clear recovery ETA estimate logic.
Automated smoke tests and chaos tests completed in staging and passed in canary region for 72 hours.
Playbook & runbook published and reviewed by SRE and Product; at least two on-call engineers signed off.
Security review completed (if required) and audit logging present for all auto-degrade decisions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): enable policy in us-west-2 on 5% of traffic for non-enterprise lanes; monitor 72h.
Phase 2 (Regional Ramp): expand to 25% across additional regions with telemetry gates and rollback thresholds.
Phase 3 (Global): enable by default for low/standard tiers, enterprise customers are default opt-in with per-customer controls.
Manual override: Console and internal API to force-enable/disable degradation for a customer or region.
Post-launch: 14-day observational window, weekly metric review for first quarter.
Rollback criteria: if post-degrade customer error_rate > 0.5% above baseline or sustained increase in user complaints for 2+ days, auto rollback and incident review.
launch_checklist: Implement metric detectors in telemetry pipeline (latency_p95, queue_depth, gpu_utilization, model_throughput).
Routing layer integration PR merged and e2e smoke tests green.
Console: toggle and visibility panel implemented; UI copy reviewed by docs.
Runbook published with step-by-step restore and postmortem template.
Synthetic workload harness updated (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) with degradation scenarios.
Customer-facing status page automation for degrade events hooked up.
On-call rotation & escalation matrix updated and paged during canary.
Stakeholder readiness: CS, Sales, Legal, and PM notified of launch timeline and messaging templates.
QA: automated tests for each degradation action and rollback path; chaos test deck executed in staging.
Telemetry dashboards and alerts created for early-warning and post-event analysis.
telemetry_and_alerting: Define metric baseline per-customer and per-lane to avoid noisy global thresholds.
Alert: 'degrade_candidate' fires when any two detectors cross thresholds within a 60s window.
Alert: 'degrade_executed' log emitted for each mitigation action with context (customer, region, model_variant).
Retention: keep detailed degrade decision logs for 90 days; surface summary metrics for 1 year.
Dashboards: per-model and per-lane views with rollback counts and customer impact quantification.
test_plan: Unit tests for routing decision logic and policy toggles.
Integration tests: simulate telemetry spikes and assert degradation actions within SLA windows.
Chaos tests: network partition / GPU slow-down scenarios to confirm fallback stability.
A/B experiment in canary: 5% traffic with policy-on vs policy-off to measure net customer impact.
Manual validation checklist for SRE to run during canary (include sample curl commands and logs to check).
risks: False positives in detectors may trigger unnecessary customer-visible degradations; mitigated by multimetric gating and short cool-downs.
Model substitution could change output distribution causing regressions in customer-facing behavior; require per-model evaluation sets before availability.
Insufficient observability could make root-cause finding slow during degradation events; prioritize dashboards first.
Enterprise customers may require stricter SLAs and opt-out flow; ensure per-customer override exists before global rollout.
